subject.title: Session lane starvation: followup drain monopolizes session lane, blocks inbound dispatch for 20-30min

question: Should OpenClaw make foreground user/control work structurally outrank background and follow-up drain work on the same session lane, and what preemption/yield policy should enforce that?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent behavior affects transcript ordering, cancellation semantics, background work guarantees, and session-state safety across all channels.

options.title: Adopt foreground-priority scheduling
options.body: Make fresh user/control turns able to interrupt, yield, or overtake background/follow-up drain work with explicit ordering and cancellation tests.

options.title: Cap follow-up drain only
options.body: Bound consecutive follow-up turns or elapsed drain time without introducing broader background/user lane separation.

options.title: Keep current semantics
options.body: Treat long waits as operational tuning/recovery issues and avoid changing same-session scheduling semantics for now.

recommendation.title: Adopt foreground-priority scheduling
recommendation.body: Make fresh user/control turns able to interrupt, yield, or overtake background/follow-up drain work with explicit ordering and cancellation tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the same reply queue and foreground-delivery boundary makes steipete the best available owner for the policy call.
